SECOND ARCHIVE PASS, 2026-08-24: Sprint 16 (BL-569..BL-578) and Sprint 17b (BL-596..BL-604) both closed on this date, and their nineteen completed items moved to archive/backlog-complete-2026-08-24.json. The hot file is EMPTY, which is the resting state this convention intends between sprints — the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs rather than inherited. (Sprint 17's own eleven items are RETAINED here by the merge of 2026-08-24: that sprint closed under the other reading of this note, with prose archived and metadata kept, and this merge does not re-archive another session's bookkeeping.)
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.design: Ruled 2026-08-25 (Ben, looking at the live Throughput lens): "when a lens needs a legend, it takes the minimap space" — the flush-left-of-the-minimap anchor is retired, because it put the key over the always-open Selection band and read as sloppy. Design settled in docs/ui/LENSES.md § legend chromes; read it before implementing. Scope: move the gradient-bar chrome (begin_lens_key) into the minimap rect and let the minimap yield; the count-driven keys already sit in the right chrome column above the minimap and should be reconciled to the same rule rather than left as a second idiom. Two consequences fall out and are deliberately part of this item: the BL-376 foreground-list + opaque-fill workaround becomes unnecessary once the legend owns its rect (it was the right fix for the wrong layout), which also dissolves the standing defect that six of the seven gradient keys were unreadable under the band; and the item must answer what the minimap does while displaced — hidden outright, or restored the moment the lens clears. A live click is required, per the UI rule. CANCELLED 2026-08-25, by Ben on seeing the merged build: "Looks fantastic, probably better than my direct instruction to fill minimap space." Sprint 17b had already moved every legend into one chrome home — the minimap HEADER, growing upward into the column — which answers the complaint that prompted the ruling (a key popped out over the Selection band) without taking the minimap's own rect. The 2026-08-25 ruling is therefore superseded by its own author in favour of what shipped. The z-order half of this item is also moot: 17b's region overlaps no window, so the foreground-list workaround was dropped at the merge rather than generalised. RENUMBERED BL-604 -> BL-609 on 2026-08-25. Sprint 17b and Sprint 18 ran concurrently on 2026-08-24 and both drew BL-604 from the same fresh id range for different work; 17b's landed in a FROZEN cold archive and holds the majority of live citations, so Sprint 18's id moved instead. items.title: Spawn viability sweep: measure every corporation start over the real warm start
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-26, opening the Sprint 20 design session: corporations open at 0cr (the 2026-07-06 new-charter steer) and market forces are meant to ensure profit gets made - "this is not great. It's simply always going to happen that different starts provide different opportunities, and we should be gathering data on this." His ruling: build the sweep FIRST, spawn forms wait for the data; and "there is nothing too special about player corporations, so we can use every angle to gather data" - every corp is a data point. WORK: tools/verify/spawn_viability.cpp, a live-Lua CMake-only sweep (the player_seed_sweep reasoning) generating one campaign-real world per seed (full 400-year prehistory; --lean smoke only) and running the 80-tick warm start with an app-faithful tick - cadence counter (BL-568), shared LP pool (BL-597), corp AI. Default mode SPECTATE (BL-409) so every corp including the player slot acts through the scored-utility layer and rows are comparable; --played runs the shipped warm start (player slot strategically passive); the delta separates acting from endowment. One CSV row per corp per seed: class (player-slot/rival/background), focus, nation, holdings open/close, balance open/min/close, ticks in debt, trailing-year net/qtr, strategic decisions taken (drained from the corp_decision_ring with saturation guarded), stockpile units at close, and three report-first flags (solvent/earning/active). Report-first on the road_reach_census idiom: the viability VERDICT rule is the design call the data feeds, so only vacuity, first-seed determinism (state_hash + every closing balance) and ring attribution assert. Registered ctest label "sweep" behind IO_RUN_SWEEPS. BUILT 2026-08-26 and run same-day on Linux via an extended NR-264 lib-then-link recipe (Lua 5.4.7 + sol2 3.5.0 from GitHub mirrors); first 8-seed campaign-real sweep data recorded in the session devlog and NR entries. The spawn-form design the data feeds is BL-627 (corporation spawn forms).

items.title: Corporation spawn forms: settle the shapes a start can take, against the sweep data
items.author: Ben
items.blocked_on: A design session with Ben over the spawn_viability sweep data (Ben, 2026-08-26: sweep first, forms wait for the data).
items.design: Ben, 2026-08-25 (dispatch-triage close-out): "there are a few forms for corporation starts to take" - the spawn-form design session Sprint 20 owes. Reordered by Ben 2026-08-26: the forms are settled AGAINST the BL-626 (spawn viability sweep) data, not ahead of it. Candidate forms on the table from the 2026-08-26 session, each solving viability differently, none chosen: (1) new charter (current: 0cr, lean assets - honest but needs a guaranteed early income, e.g. a seeded procurement contract on the existing contracts loop); (2) charter loan - opening capital as DEBT on the existing k_debt_interest_per_quarter mechanism, cash to act with market discipline intact; (3) established firm - larger holdings plus operating history, wealth as assets not cash; (4) backed subsidiary - a nation or parent stake, tying starts into the politics layer. Constraints carried from the close-out: every form must be one a RIVAL can bootstrap (the "never on cash" availability ruling means a corp with no stock and no market access may have no legal candidates - a form that strands rivals poisons every seed's data); relative comparison across forms on a fixed seed + rival field, absolute numbers being confounded by the open economy pathologies; one deliberate baseline re-bless wave at the end of the viability pass, with provenance, not a dribble (NR-596 precedent). The frame settled 2026-08-26 and written into CORPORATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4: viability is a FLOOR, not equality - different starts giving different opportunities is intended variety, a start dead before turn one is a defect. The verdict rule (which combination of solvent/earning/active is "viable") is part of this design, first-cut ingredients logged for Ben's review.
